title: The wrong trousers
setting: A Saturday afternoon in a clothes shop. Sora starts a new part-time job at a restaurant next week, and Mai has come along to help him find a pair of black trousers. She pulls a pair off a rail and he takes them into the fitting room, chatting with her through the curtain.

speakers.name: Mai
speakers.voice: female, late 20s, warm, a little shy

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: atarashii baito tte, kuroi zubon o haku n da yo ne?
lines.ja: 新しいバイトって、黒いズボンを履くんだよね？
lines.kana: あたらしいばいとって、くろいずぼんをはくんだよね？
lines.english: So at your new job, you wear black trousers, right?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: un. ue wa mise no fuku o kiru kedo, zubon wa jibun no o haku n da.
lines.ja: うん。上は店の服を着るけど、ズボンは自分のを履くんだ。
lines.kana: うん。うえはみせのふくをきるけど、ずぼんはじぶんのをはくんだ。
lines.english: Yeah. On top I wear what the restaurant gives us, but the trousers have to be my own.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: jaa, kore wa? sora no saizu mo aru yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、これは？ソラのサイズもあるよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、これは？そらのさいずもあるよ。
lines.english: Then how about these? They've got your size, too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: ii ne. jaa, kore, haite miru.
lines.ja: いいね。じゃあ、これ、履いてみる。
lines.kana: いいね。じゃあ、これ、はいてみる。
lines.english: Nice. OK, I'll try these on.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.english: Sora, are you changed? How are they?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: mada. are? nanka saizu awanai. hairanai yo.
lines.ja: まだ。あれ？なんかサイズ合わない。入らないよ。
lines.kana: まだ。あれ？なんかさいずあわない。はいらないよ。
lines.english: Not yet. Huh? They're not my size somehow. I can't get them on.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: e? itsumo no saizu desho? a, gomen! koko, rediisu da.
lines.ja: え？いつものサイズでしょ？あ、ごめん！ここ、レディースだ。
lines.kana: え？いつものさいずでしょ？あ、ごめん！ここ、れでぃーすだ。
lines.english: What? They're your usual size, aren't they? Oh, sorry! This is the women's section.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: rediisu? sore ja, saizu awanai wake da yo.
lines.ja: レディース？それじゃ、サイズ合わないわけだよ。
lines.kana: れでぃーす？それじゃ、さいずあわないわけだよ。
lines.english: Women's? Well, no wonder they don't fit!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: gomen gomen. hai, menzu no zubon motte kita. kore, haite mite.
lines.ja: ごめんごめん。はい、メンズのズボン持ってきた。これ、履いてみて。
lines.kana: ごめんごめん。はい、めんずのずぼんもってきた。これ、はいてみて。
lines.english: Sorry, sorry. Here, I've brought you some men's trousers. Try these on.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: a, kore wa saizu atteru. dou? niau?
lines.ja: あ、これはサイズ合ってる。どう？似合う？
lines.kana: あ、これはさいずあってる。どう？にあう？
lines.english: Oh, these fit. What do you think? Do they suit me?

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, niau niau! sora, sutairu ii kara, nandemo niau ne.
lines.ja: うん、似合う似合う！ソラ、スタイルいいから、何でも似合うね。
lines.kana: うん、にあうにあう！そら、すたいるいいから、なんでもにあうね。
lines.english: Yeah, they really suit you! You've got such a good figure, everything looks good on you.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, kore ni suru. fuku kigaete kuru ne.
lines.ja: じゃあ、これにする。服着替えてくるね。
lines.kana: じゃあ、これにする。ふくきがえてくるね。
lines.english: Then I'll get these. I'll go and change back.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un. nee, sakki no rediisu no zubon, kawaikatta yo ne.
lines.ja: うん。ねえ、さっきのレディースのズボン、かわいかったよね。
lines.kana: うん。ねえ、さっきのれでぃーすのずぼん、かわいかったよね。
lines.english: OK. Hey, those women's trousers from before were cute, weren't they?

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: jaa, mai ga haite mitara? mai ni wa zettai niau yo.
lines.ja: じゃあ、マイが履いてみたら？マイには絶対似合うよ。
lines.kana: じゃあ、まいがはいてみたら？まいにはぜったいにあうよ。
lines.english: So why don't you try them on? They'd definitely suit you.

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: honto? jaa, watashi mo chotto kigaete kuru.
lines.ja: ほんと？じゃあ、私もちょっと着替えてくる。
lines.kana: ほんと？じゃあ、わたしもちょっときがえてくる。
lines.english: Really? OK, I'll go and change too.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.ja: マイ、どう？ほら、似合うじゃん！
lines.kana: まい、どう？ほら、にあうじゃん！
lines.english: Mai, how are they? See? They look great on you!

lines.speaker: mai
lines.romaji: un, saizu mo atteru shi, ki ni itta! kore kau.
lines.ja: うん、サイズも合ってるし、気に入った！これ買う。
lines.kana: うん、さいずもあってるし、きにいった！これかう。
lines.english: Yeah, and they're my size, too. I love them! I'm getting these.

lines.speaker: sora
lines.romaji: e, mai mo kau no? boku no zubon o kai ni kita noni.
lines.ja: え、マイも買うの？僕のズボンを買いに来たのに。
lines.kana: え、まいもかうの？ぼくのずぼんをかいにきたのに。
lines.english: Wait, you're buying some too? We came here to buy MY trousers!

choices.english: Sora's usual size was too small, so Mai found him a bigger size, and he bought those.
Mai handed Sora women's trousers by mistake. He took a men's pair that fit, and Mai decided to buy the women's pair.
Mai picked out black trousers for Sora, but he decided to wear the restaurant's trousers instead.

questions.explanation: Line 7: Mai realises they're in the women's section (koko, rediisu da), so the pair she gave Sora was women's, and that's why he couldn't get them on (line 6: saizu awanai, hairanai; line 8: saizu awanai wake da). In line 9 she brings men's trousers, they fit (line 10), and he takes them (line 12: kore ni suru). Then Mai tries on the women's pair and buys it (line 17: kore kau), and Sora jokes that they came to buy his trousers (line 18). A is wrong: the first pair was his usual size, and the problem was that it was women's; Mai brought men's trousers, not a bigger size. A also leaves out Mai buying a pair. C is wrong: in line 2 Sora says the restaurant gives him the top, but the trousers have to be his own.

questions.english: Sora explains what he wears at his new job. What did he say about the trousers?
questions.ja: ソラは、ズボンのことを何と言いましたか？
questions.kana: そらは、ずぼんのことをなんといいましたか？
questions.romaji: sora wa, zubon no koto o nan to iimashita ka?

choices.english: the trousers, I wear (kiru) my own
choices.romaji: zubon wa jibun no o kiru n da

choices.english: the trousers, I put on (tsukeru) my own
choices.romaji: zubon wa jibun no o tsukeru n da

choices.english: the trousers, I wear (haku) my own
choices.romaji: zubon wa jibun no o haku n da

questions.explanation: Line 2: 'zubon wa jibun no o haku n da'. Trousers take haku, the same verb as shoes, because you step into them. In the same line Sora uses kiru for the top (ue wa mise no fuku o kiru), so you hear the two verbs side by side. Mai uses haku too: 'kuroi zubon o haku' in line 1 and 'haite mite' (try them on) in line 9. A is the English speaker's trap: kiru is for things on the upper body, like shirts and jackets, not trousers. B is wrong: tsukeru is for accessories such as a necklace or a watch, not trousers.

questions.english: Sora comes to pick you up for dinner just as you get home from work, still in your work clothes. He says, "onaka suita! sugu gohan ni ikou yo." Tell him you'll just go and get changed first.
questions.ja: お腹すいた！すぐご飯に行こうよ。
questions.kana: おなかすいた！すぐごはんにいこうよ。
questions.romaji: onaka suita! sugu gohan ni ikou yo.
questions.answer: Say you'll go and change with kigaeru, usually as kigaete kuru (go, get changed and come back). fuku can stay or be dropped, and you can ask him to wait with chotto matte.

modelAnswers.romaji: chotto matte. fuku kigaete kuru ne.
modelAnswers.ja: ちょっと待って。服着替えてくるね。
modelAnswers.english: Hang on. I'll just go and get changed.

modelAnswers.romaji: ii yo. demo saki ni kigaete kuru kara, chotto mattete.
modelAnswers.ja: いいよ。でも先に着替えてくるから、ちょっと待ってて。
modelAnswers.english: Sure. But I'll get changed first, so wait a sec.

questions.explanation: Sora says 'fuku kigaete kuru ne' in line 12, and Mai says 'watashi mo chotto kigaete kuru' in line 15: the -te kuru form means you go, do it, and come back. Mai's 'kigaeta?' in line 5 (are you changed?) shows that fuku is often left out, because kigaeru already means changing clothes. Don't say fuku o kaeru: that's about switching to a different outfit, not getting changed. Sora is a friend speaking casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: You're out shopping with Mai. She comes out of the fitting room in a new jacket, turns around and asks, "dou kana, kore?" Tell her it suits her.
questions.answer: Say it suits her with niau. In casual speech ga drops and so does the noun: niau yo, or yoku niatteru (it really suits you). sugoku adds emphasis.

modelAnswers.ja: いいね！よく似合ってるよ。
modelAnswers.english: Nice! It looks great on you.

questions.explanation: In line 11 Mai tells Sora 'niau niau!', and in line 16 Sora tells Mai 'hora, niau jan!' when she comes out in the women's trousers. niau is about how something looks on a person. Whether it's the right size is a different phrase, saizu ga au: in line 10 Sora checks both, one after the other (saizu atteru. dou? niau?). A shop assistant, or anyone speaking politely, says 'yoku oniai desu ne'. Mai asks casually, so answer casually.

questions.english: When Sora tries on the men's trousers, he says, "a, kore wa saizu atteru." What does he mean?
questions.ja: メンズのズボンは、どうでしたか？
questions.kana: めんずのずぼんは、どうでしたか？
questions.romaji: menzu no zubon wa, dou deshita ka?

choices.english: These go well with my top.

questions.explanation: Line 10: 'a, kore wa saizu atteru'. With saizu as the subject, au (here atteru) means the size is right: unlike the women's pair, which wasn't his size and wouldn't go on (line 6: saizu awanai, hairanai), these fit. B is wrong: 'looks good on me' is niau, which Sora asks about straight after, as a separate question (dou? niau?). C is wrong: au can mean 'go with' when one thing matches another, but Sora is talking about the size, not about what the trousers go with.
